      10 Best Beaches in Lombok: From Pink Sand Shores to Secret Coves

      by Team Out of Town about 20 hours ago 151 Views

      10 Most Beautiful Beaches in Lombok for Your Next Indonesian Island Escape

      When I think about Indonesian islands that still feel exciting to explore, Lombok immediately comes to mind. While Bali has long been the country’s international beach icon, Lombok offers something increasingly rare: spectacular coastlines that still feel wild, spacious, and wonderfully uncrowded. Here, the scenery changes dramatically from one beach to another. One moment, you can be standing on a rare shoreline tinged with pink; an hour later, you may find yourself looking at a perfect crescent of white sand framed by green hills.

      The southern part of the island is particularly rewarding for beach lovers, with a string of beautiful bays around Kuta and Mandalika. Eastern Lombok adds another dimension with its famous Pink Beach, while quieter corners of the island offer secluded stretches for travelers willing to explore beyond the main tourist routes. Tanjung Aan, Selong Belanak and Mawun are among the most accessible highlights, while beaches such as Mawi, Tampah and Semeti appeal to travelers looking for a wilder side of Lombok.

      Here are some of the best beaches in Lombok, from famous postcard-perfect shores to beautiful secret coves.

      1. Pink Beach (Pantai Tangsi)

      Pink Beach is undoubtedly one of the most unusual and memorable beaches in Lombok. Located on the island’s southeastern coast, this beautiful stretch of shoreline is famous for its subtly rosy-colored sand, created by pale sand mixed with fragments of red coral.

      food
      Hotel

      The intensity of the pink can vary with sunlight, weather, and sand moisture, so visiting at different times of day can yield surprisingly different views. The combination of pink-tinted sand, turquoise water, and rugged hills makes the beach feel unlike many of Indonesia’s more familiar tropical coastlines. The surrounding area is also relatively remote, which adds to the sense of adventure.

      I would recommend coming here with enough time to explore rather than treating it as a quick photo stop. Bring water, snacks, and sun protection, as facilities can be more limited than at the beaches near Kuta. Pink Beach is generally reached by private car, scooter, or organized tour.

      From Kuta Lombok, the journey takes roughly 1.5 to 2 hours depending on traffic and road conditions. From central or western Lombok, hiring a private driver is often the more comfortable option. The long journey becomes part of the experience as the road passes villages and quieter rural landscapes before finally reaching this extraordinary shoreline.

      2. Tanjung Aan Beach

      Tanjung Aan is one of those beaches that immediately explains why Lombok has become such a favorite among travelers looking beyond Bali. Located east of Kuta in South Lombok, it features a sweeping bay with bright turquoise water, pale sand, and green hills rising around the coastline. What makes Tanjung Aan particularly interesting is the changing texture of its sand. Parts of the beach have the fine, powdery sand that travelers expect from a tropical postcard, while another section is known for its coarser, pepper-like grains.

      The beach is large enough that it rarely feels as confined as many famous beaches elsewhere in Southeast Asia. You can spend time swimming, relaxing under the sun, walking along the shoreline, or simply enjoying a fresh coconut from one of the small local stalls. One of the best ways to appreciate its beauty is to view it from the surrounding viewpoints. A short walk up Bukit Merese or nearby hills reveals wide views of the curving coastline and the Indian Ocean beyond.

      Tanjung Aan is one of the easiest beaches to visit from Kuta Lombok. It is approximately 10 kilometers east of town and can generally be reached in around 15 to 25 minutes by scooter or private car.

      The road is relatively straightforward compared with access routes to some of Lombok’s more remote beaches, making Tanjung Aan an excellent choice for first-time visitors.

      3. Selong Belanak Beach

      If I had to recommend one Lombok beach that appeals to almost every kind of traveler, Selong Belanak would be near the top of the list. Located on the island’s southern coast, this spectacular beach forms a broad crescent surrounded by rolling green hills. The pale sand is soft and inviting, while the wide bay gives the scenery a wonderfully open feeling. It is beautiful in photographs, but the real charm of Selong Belanak is how easy it is to enjoy all day.

      The beach is particularly popular with beginner surfers because gentle waves and a sandy bottom make it one of the more approachable places in South Lombok to learn. Surf schools and board rentals can be found nearby, while non-surfers can simply enjoy the calmer sections of the bay. Families, couples and solo travelers can all find their own corner along the long shoreline. In the late afternoon, the combination of low sunlight, green hills and traditional coastal life creates a particularly beautiful atmosphere.

      Selong Belanak is west of Kuta Lombok and is generally accessible by scooter, private car, or driver.  Travel times vary depending on the route and starting point, but the trip from Kuta typically takes around 45 to 55 minutes. It is also possible to combine Selong Belanak with Mawun and other beaches in South Lombok in a day of coastal exploration.

      4. Mawun Beach

      Mawun Beach is one of my favorite examples of Lombok’s ability to surprise travelers. From the road, there is little indication that such a beautiful bay is waiting ahead. Then the landscape opens to reveal a near-perfect horseshoe-shaped beach framed by green hills on both sides. Located along the southern coast, Mawun feels more secluded than some of the island’s better-known beaches, making it an excellent choice for travelers who want scenery without the energy of a busy surf destination.

      The beach itself is beautifully simple. Soft, pale sand meets clear blue water, while the bay’s curve creates a natural sense of shelter. The surrounding hills provide a dramatic backdrop, making Mawun especially attractive for photography. It is a wonderful place to slow down, swim near the shore when conditions are suitable, read a book, or simply listen to the waves. There is relatively little development compared with beaches closer to Kuta, and that lack of commercial activity is part of its appeal.

      Mawun Beach is located west of Kuta Lombok and is easiest to reach by scooter, private car or hired driver. The journey generally takes around 30 to 45 minutes, depending on your starting point and road conditions. The final approach can feel more remote than the road to Tanjung Aan, but the reward is a beach that still retains a peaceful, almost hidden quality.

      5. Tampah Beach

      Tampah Beach is a wonderful choice for travelers searching for a quieter side of South Lombok. Less internationally famous than Tanjung Aan or Selong Belanak, this beautiful coastal area rewards those willing to venture slightly beyond the island’s most obvious attractions. The beach has soft sand, clear water, and a more relaxed atmosphere, while the surrounding hills and undeveloped coastline create a sense that you have stumbled upon one of Lombok’s better-kept secrets.

      What I particularly like about beaches such as Tampah is that they encourage travelers to slow down. There is less pressure to rush between famous landmarks or search for the perfect social-media photograph. Instead, the experience is about enjoying the coastline itself. Depending on where you stop, you may find relatively few people, especially outside busy weekends and holidays. The views from the surrounding coastal roads can also be spectacular, with green slopes meeting the blue waters of the Indian Ocean.

      Tampah Beach is located along Lombok’s southern coastline and is generally explored from Kuta. The most practical way to reach it is by scooter or private vehicle, though travelers unfamiliar with Lombok’s roads may prefer to hire a local driver. Some access roads to quieter beaches can be rougher or less clearly marked, so it is wise to check current local conditions before leaving. Tampah can also be included as part of a longer South Lombok beach-hopping itinerary.

      6. Mawi Beach

      Mawi Beach is for travelers who prefer their coastal scenery a little wilder. Located on Lombok’s southern coast, Mawi is known for its powerful surf, dramatic headlands, and remote atmosphere. This is not the kind of beach where everyone arrives to float casually in calm water. Instead, it is a place where the natural landscape takes center stage. Darker volcanic sand, rugged cliffs, and energetic waves give Mawi a distinctly different character from the gentle bays of Selong Belanak and Mawun.

      For experienced surfers, Mawi is one of the island’s more exciting destinations. The reef break can produce powerful waves, and conditions are better suited to confident surfers than beginners. Even travelers who do not surf, however, may enjoy visiting simply to experience the scenery. The cliffs and hills surrounding the beach create a dramatic sense of isolation, and on quieter days the coastline can feel almost completely untouched.

      Getting to Mawi is part of the adventure. It is accessible from Kuta Lombok by scooter or private vehicle, but the final approach may involve rougher, steeper roads than the main routes to popular beaches. Confident scooter riders may enjoy the journey, while others may be more comfortable hiring a local driver. Bring enough drinking water and basic supplies, as facilities can be limited.

      7. Semeti Beach

      Semeti Beach is one of Lombok’s most dramatic hidden coastal landscapes. It is not the classic white-sand beach where you spend hours swimming and sunbathing. Instead, Semeti is known for its rugged geological formations, rocky shoreline, and striking sea views. For adventurous travelers and photographers, that makes it one of the most interesting places along the South Lombok coast.

      The beach’s character comes from the dramatic rocks that rise around the shoreline. Depending on the angle and lighting, the landscape can look almost otherworldly, especially when waves crash against the formations. The surrounding coastline is also less developed than the main tourist beaches around Kuta, which adds to the feeling of discovery. Sunset and early morning can be particularly rewarding for photography, although visitors should always be cautious around wet rocks and strong waves.

      Semeti is generally reached from Kuta Lombok by scooter or private vehicle. Unlike Tanjung Aan and Selong Belanak, the route can involve rougher roads and less straightforward access. Local advice is valuable, particularly after heavy rain, when unpaved tracks may become more challenging to navigate. I would recommend combining Semeti with other lesser-known beaches on the eastern side of South Lombok and allowing plenty of time for the journey rather than rushing.

      8. Kuta Beach, Lombok

      Kuta Beach is the easiest beach to visit for travelers staying in Lombok’s popular southern tourism hub. Located close to the town of Kuta and the Mandalika area, it may not feel as secluded as Mawun or as unusual as Pink Beach, but its accessibility makes it an excellent introduction to the island’s coastline. The long beach offers plenty of space for walking, while the surrounding hills and the developing Mandalika landscape provide an attractive backdrop.

      What makes Kuta Beach appealing is its convenience. You can spend time by the water, then quickly return to nearby restaurants, cafés, and accommodations. It is particularly suitable for travelers who want to enjoy Lombok’s beaches without spending every day on a scooter or in a car. The atmosphere also provides an interesting contrast to the quieter beaches farther away. Kuta is where you can feel the island’s growing tourism scene while still being close to some of its most spectacular natural attractions.

      If you are staying in Kuta Lombok, getting to the beach is very easy. Depending on your accommodation, you may be able to walk or take a very short scooter or car ride. Travelers arriving from Lombok International Airport can reach Kuta by private transfer, taxi or other transport options before using the town as a base for exploring nearby beaches.

      9. Sire Beach

      For a change of scenery from Lombok’s dramatic southern coast, head north to Sire Beach. Located near the northwestern part of the island and within easy reach of the Gili Islands area, Sire offers a calmer and more relaxed beach experience. The water is generally gentler than the open southern coastline, while the long stretch of sand and tropical surroundings make it suitable for travelers who simply want to swim, relax, and enjoy views across the sea.

      Sire Beach is particularly appealing to families and travelers who prefer calm water over powerful surf. The atmosphere is quieter and less adventurous than the southern beaches, but that is precisely its charm. On a clear day, the surrounding seascape can be spectacular, and the beach provides a pleasant alternative for travelers exploring northern Lombok or preparing to visit the nearby Gili Islands.

      The easiest way to reach Sire Beach depends on where you are staying. Travelers coming from Senggigi or other parts of western Lombok can hire a private car or driver, while those staying in northern Lombok may find the journey relatively short. Scooter  travel is possible for experienced riders, although a private car is more comfortable for longer distances.

      10. Nipah Beach

      Nipah Beach is a beautiful option for travelers exploring Lombok’s western and northern coastline. Compared with the famous beaches around Kuta, Nipah has a more relaxed atmosphere and is convenient for visitors staying near Senggigi. The beach is known for its attractive bay, clear water, and peaceful coastal scenery, making it a pleasant choice for travelers seeking a slower beach day without traveling deep into South Lombok.

      Book Vacation Rentals

      One of Nipah’s biggest strengths is its atmosphere. The coastline feels less focused on surfing and more suited to swimming, relaxing, and enjoying the tropical surroundings. The beach is particularly appealing later in the day, when the light softens, and the coastal views become more atmospheric. It is also a convenient place to combine a beach visit with exploring nearby restaurants and other attractions along Lombok’s western coast.

      Nipah Beach is generally reached by road from Senggigi and other western parts of Lombok. A private car, hired driver, or scooter is the most convenient way to get there, depending on your confidence and travel plans. Its location makes Nipah an easy addition to a western Lombok itinerary and a good choice for travelers who do not have time to explore the more distant beaches in the south or east.

      Frequently Asked Questions About Lombok’s Best Beaches

      What is the most beautiful beach in Lombok?

      Tanjung Aan is often considered one of Lombok’s most beautiful all-around beaches because of its turquoise water, distinctive sand, and spectacular surrounding hills. However, Pink Beach is the most unusual, while Mawun offers one of the most beautiful secluded bay settings.

      Where is Pink Beach in Lombok?

      Pink Beach, also known as Pantai Tangsi, is located on the southeastern side of Lombok. It is best reached by private car, scooter, or organized tour and is usually visited as a longer day trip from Kuta Lombok.

      What is the best beach in Lombok for swimming?

      Mawun, Selong Belanak, and calmer sections of Tanjung Aan are popular choices for swimming when sea conditions are suitable. Always check local conditions, tides, and currents before entering the water.

      Which Lombok beach is best for beginner surfers?

      Selong Belanak is one of the best choices for beginners because of its approachable waves, sandy bottom, and availability of surf schools and board rentals.

      How many days do you need to explore Lombok’s beaches?

      A minimum of three days allows you to visit several major beaches around Kuta and South Lombok. Five to seven days is better if you also want to explore Pink Beach, northern beaches, and other parts of the island without rushing.

      What is the best time to visit Lombok’s beaches?

      The dry season generally offers more consistently sunny weather and is a popular time for beach exploration. Conditions can vary between beaches, however, especially on the south coast where waves and currents may be stronger depending on the season.

      Is Lombok better than Bali for beaches?

      That depends on what you want. Bali offers more beach clubs, restaurants, and tourism infrastructure, while Lombok is often more appealing to travelers seeking wider beaches, quieter scenery, surfing, and a stronger sense of discovery.

      Can you explore Lombok’s beaches by scooter?

      Yes, many of the major beaches around Kuta, including Tanjung Aan and Selong Belanak, are accessible by scooter. However, some remote beaches have rougher roads, so travelers who are not confident riding on uneven terrain may prefer to hire a local driver.

      Final Thoughts

      Lombok’s coastline is best explored with a sense of curiosity. The island rewards travelers who do more than simply visit its most famous beach and leave. Start with the turquoise waters of Tanjung Aan, learn to surf at Selong Belanak, enjoy the peaceful curve of Mawun, and then venture farther toward Pink Beach or the rugged hidden coastline around Semeti and Mawi.

      For me, that is the real appeal of Lombok: every beach feels like it offers a slightly different version of the island. Some are polished and easy to reach, while others require patience, rough roads, and a willingness to explore. From rare pink sand to quiet crescent bays, Lombok remains one of Indonesia’s most rewarding destinations for travelers who love discovering new places.
